title: Waterloo Town Square expropriation and Shakespeare Drive tender
subtitle: Neighbourhood and sports community reports, Woolwich Street widening by-law, demolition control summary and joint services update.
overview: Council approved the expropriation of land at the Waterloo Town Square north parking lot, after considering the Ontario Land Tribunal's report on the hearing of necessity {{vote:m8}}. It also awarded the Shakespeare Drive reconstruction tender to Oxford Civil Group Inc. for a total of $2,883,616.88, including unrecoverable HST {{vote:m7}}.

Council received annual reports on neighbourhood community building and on sports and recreation community development and grants. Demolition control and Joint Service Initiatives Committee reports were also received on the consent motion. Questions focused on neighbourhoods with fewer supports, multi-unit buildings, and funding for a seniors program that relies on a provincial grant ending March 31.

Council also passed a by-law to establish a widening of Woolwich Street as a public highway {{vote:m9}}. The meeting began with a closed session on a labour matter and a land transaction; the minutes report no public outcome from it.

decisions.item: Waterloo Town Square north parking lot expropriation
decisions.detail: Council approved expropriating the identified lands for municipal purposes including the Town Square master plan, and authorized staff to carry out the required expropriation steps and offers of compensation.
Council awarded RFT26-02 to Oxford Civil Group Inc. for a total of $2,883,616.88 including unrecoverable HST, and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the agreement.
Council received report COM2026-004 for information.

decisions.item: Sports and recreation community development summary
decisions.detail: Council received report COM2026-005 on 2025 community development and grant support for information.
Council received report CAO2026-001 for information.

debate: On neighbourhood work, one councillor asked about gaps; staff said some areas lack associations, connectors or grant applicants, and have added pop-ups and outreach in those areas.
Councillors raised multi-unit buildings as a community-building challenge. Staff pointed to the neighbourhood connector program and mini grants as low-barrier ways to take part.

One councillor said some long-running Uptown events ended because of permit processes, and that events outgrowing a neighbourhood scale fall into a gap. Staff said some requirements cannot be removed but they help groups with applications, and offered a follow-up discussion.
On the seniors program in multi-unit buildings, staff said the provincial grant ends March 31, the staff role was temporarily extended, and other provincial funding has been applied for.

On sports grants, a councillor asked whether girls' youth sports got a fair share. Staff said applications are assessed on several criteria, including financial position. Councillors also asked about water fill stations at sports fields, and staff said availability depends on whether a site has water service.
